summary: The character is trivial on σ of K(g)-elements divided by g, and σ is additive on 𝖲 and vanishes on 𝖧.

steps.claim: Let k = u⁻¹(h⁻¹vh) ∈ K(g). Since K(g) = unitaryLevel(Ô, g), g⁻¹σ(k) ∈ Ô, so selfDualChar(g⁻¹σ(k)) = 1. Hence unipotentChar(u) = unipotentChar(u)·selfDualChar(g⁻¹σ(k)) = selfDualChar(g⁻¹(σ(u) + σ(k))) = selfDualChar(g⁻¹σ(uk)) (σ is additive on 𝖲, simpleRootSum_mul) and uk = h⁻¹vh with σ(h⁻¹vh) = σ(v) (σ vanishes on h, h⁻¹ ∈ 𝖧); so unipotentChar(u) = unipotentChar(v).

  ← S.selfDualChar.map_add_eq_mul, ← mul_add, ← simpleRootSum_mul] <;> grind [unipotentChar,
